source: R package ChainLadder, vignette 'ChainLadder' (Gesmann et al.), https://mages.github.io/ChainLadder/articles/ChainLadder.html, section 'Mack chain-ladder', call as printed: MackChainLadder(RAA, est.sigma="Mack")
est_sigma_note: The vignette output transcribed here uses est.sigma="Mack" (Mack's 1993 min-rule for the last sigma). The package DEFAULT is est.sigma="log-linear": it regresses log(sigma_k) on k over the estimable k and extrapolates the last sigma, and falls back to the Mack rule only when the regression slope p-value exceeds 0.05. The two rules give different values for the last sigma on RAA; see CASE_STUDY.md.
cross_check: Mack (1994), CAS Forum Spring 1994 pp. 101-182, p. 130 prints the same per-year table (C_i10, R_i, s.e.(R_i), s.e./R_i) with the same digits and the alpha_k^2 row 27883 1109 691 61.2 119 40.8 1.34 7.88 and alpha_9^2 = 1.34 by the min-rule, noting that the log-linear extrapolation would give exp(-0.44) = 0.64 instead. https://www.casact.org/sites/default/files/2021-03/7_Mack_1994.pdf

default_rule_totals.source: https://mages.github.io/ChainLadder/reference/summary.MackChainLadder.html (call MackChainLadder(Triangle = RAA), no est.sigma argument, so the default log-linear rule) and https://mages.github.io/ChainLadder/reference/MackChainLadder.html (mse.method='Mack' gives Mack S.E. 26880.74; mse.method='Independence' gives 26895.69)
default_rule_totals.note: Per-origin rows under the default rule are not transcribed (the page renders them, the fetch returned only the totals). Only Mack.S.E and CV differ from the est.sigma='Mack' output.
